title.narrative: Provision of life-saving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene support for drought affected and vulnerable families in Xudur district of Bakool region

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia’s Federal Government officially declared a national drought emergency on 10 November 2025, following the failure of the Deyr (October–December) rains and four consecutive seasons of low precipitation. This declaration, endorsed by federal member states at the Somalia Humanitarian Forum in Jowhar, underscored that 4.4 million people were imminently at risk of food insecurity and 1.85 million children under five could suffer acute malnutrition. The drought has severely impacted water sources with over 170 boreholes and shallow wells non-functional and 4.1 million people water insecure. Water prices have surged, food scarcity is worsening, and livestock deaths are widespread, leading to collapsing livelihoods. Forecasts for early 2026 predict continued dry conditions and extreme heat, increasing the risk of crop failure and deepening humanitarian needs.ltbrgtIn Xudur District, Bakool region, the situation is critical. FAO SWALIM reports severe to extreme drought, with sharp reductions in pasture, surface water, and soil moisture. Communities—especially IDPs, women, children, and persons with disabilities—face acute water shortages, high livestock mortality, and increased risk of disease outbreaks. Schools and health facilities are also struggling to maintain basic WASH servicesltbrgtTo address these urgent needs, the project will provide life-saving WASH assistance to 10,000 people (2000 men, 6000 women, 1000 boys and 1000 girls) . Key interventions include Rehabilitation of 6 flood-proof shallow wells. ARD will also construct 10 emergency latrines in villages 4 of it for PLWD.1600 Households will benefit from hygiene kit distribution and hygiene awareness, Chlorination of 12 Shallow wells and WASH committees will be established in addition to carrying out environmental sanitation services to all project target locations especially IDP camps to improve all preventive measures against the risks of AWD/cholera outbreaks in Xudur district. ARD will also implement Water treatment and monitoring through chlorination of communal water sources. Garbage collection and clean campaigns will be conducted a cross targeted locations especially in the IDPs camps in Xudur district. Protection and inclusion will be integrated throughout, ensuring gender- and disability-sensitive approaches, privacy during service delivery, and GBV referral pathways. Staff and volunteers will be trained in safeguarding and PSEA principles. The project will coordinate closely with WASH and CCCM Clusters and link with nutrition, education, and protection interventions to maximize impact and avoid duplication.ltbrgtThe main activities will include:ltbrgtRehabilitation of 6 shallow wells with hand pumps in Waaney villageltbrgtProvision of emergency water supply targeting 6,000 vulnerable IDP beneficiaries in Waaney ,Tuboy,Gaabaney and kontomo VillagesltbrgtWater treatment and monitoring through chlorination of communal water sources targeting 12 shallow wellsltbrgtConstruction of 10 new emergency latrines with proper hand washing facilities and 4 latrines for people living with disabilities for Target Villages( Tuboy,Waney and Gaabanye Villages in Xudur district.lt/pgtltpgtProvision of 80 sanitation tools kits to support 32 clean up solid waste management activities such as garbage collection and clean campaigns for all Targeted locations in Xudur district.ltbrgtDistribution of 1600 hygiene kits including standard MHM sets and hygiene promotion campaigns targeting communities and the kits will be procured. lt/pgtltpgtARD will procure 3 water/bladders (10,000L)to support safe and reliable water storage at water trucking sites in xudur district.lt/pgt
